intent: Existing local and project chats stay reachable after the chat-first shell lands, and importing one never touches the database it came from.
steps: Start from an installation that already holds local sessions in app data and project sessions in a project folder's own store.
Open the chat-first shell with no folder granted and inspect the unified history list.
Confirm each legacy project chat whose folder is not currently granted is hidden rather than shown as broken.
Grant the exact folder that owns one legacy project chat and open that chat through the compatibility path.
Run the explicit import that copies that legacy conversation into app-private history.
Inspect the imported conversation's owner metadata and the original source database on disk.
Revoke the folder grant again and re-inspect the history list.
expectedOutcome: Local sessions remain ordinary history and stay visible without any folder grant.
A legacy project chat becomes readable through the compatibility path only after its exact canonical folder is granted.
The explicit import copies the conversation into app-private history while preserving its original owner metadata.
The source database is byte-identical before and after the import.
After revocation the imported copy stays readable and the legacy original returns to hidden.
History discovery is unified in the new shell without a Project concept appearing for fresh users.
mustNotHappen: No migration or import deletes, rewrites, moves, or destructively merges the source database.
A legacy project chat is never revealed, indexed, or read before its exact folder is granted.
Plume never searches arbitrary disk locations or performs automatic project discovery to find a legacy store.
A hidden legacy chat never surfaces its content, path, or folder identity in the history list.
Removing the Projects surface never deletes a chat, a folder store, an approval ledger, or an accepted-source manifest.
